concurrency_and_state: PlayerService.gI() uses volatile DCL singleton, whereas SkillService.gI() (lines 37-42) uses unsynchronized non-volatile lazy initialization (race on startup).

PlayerService.hoiSinh() (lines 269-298) performs check-then-act on player.isDie(), lastTimeRevived, and gold/gem deduction without locking player or inventory, risking double-revive or double-deduction under concurrent requests.

SkillService.useSkillAttack() / useSkillAlone() mutate playerSkill state (prepareQCKK, prepareLaze, prepareTuSat, lastTimeUseThisSkill, lastTimeAttack) without synchronization; Boss/Pet TU_SAT schedules explodeTuSat() on GameLoopManager (lines 761-769) which can race with Zone/Session threads.

SkillService iterates player.zone.mobs, getHumanoids(), getNotBosses(), getBosses(), and player.newSkill.playersTaget/mobsTaget across combat methods without synchronization (depends on Zone returning snapshot copies to avoid ConcurrentModificationException).

PlayerService.playerMove() mutates player.location.x/y and player.isFly without synchronization; SkillService.updateSkillSpecial() hits all targets in range on every tick while stepSkillSpecial == 1 without per-cast hit deduplication.
cross_module_questions: Does Message.cleanup() handle double-calls safely (SkillService.learSkillSpecial calls it twice at lines 377 and 382), and does Player.sendMessage() clean up Message on error when callers like PlayerService.sendInfoHpMpMoney (lines 123-141) omit msg.cleanup()?

In Client Unity C# Controller, how is Message(-60) parsed when useSkillBuffToPlayer writes byte(0) at line 869 vs playerAttackPlayer writing byte(1), byte(0), int(dameHit), boolean(isDie), boolean(isCrit) at lines 1071-1079?
Does NPoint.setHp/setHP/addHp/addMp enforce [0, hpMax] bounds and thread safety, and why does SkillService.useSkillAttack (line 440) wrap HP in Util.maxIntValue() while NPoint supports long HP?
Why were SUPER_KAME, LIEN_HOAN_CHUONG, MA_PHONG_BA removed from SkillService.useNewSkillNotFocus (line 226), leaving updateSkillSpecial and newSkillNotFocus partly orphaned/dead-pathed?
Does Zone.getHumanoids() / getNotBosses() / getBosses() / mobs return thread-safe snapshots or live lists?

db_redis_touchpoints.op: UPDATE account set ban = 1 where id = ? and username = ?
db_redis_touchpoints.safety_note: Parameterized via AlyraManager.executeUpdate (no SQL injection), but runs synchronously on caller thread (blocking I/O), lacks null-check on playerBaned.getSession(), and silently swallows exceptions.

findings.impact: Casting Tri Thuong heals enemy/PvP players in 300px range and multiplies the caster's own HP/MP heal by the number of targets in the AoE.
findings.root_cause: In useSkillBuffToPlayer (TRI_THUONG), line 857 checks canHsPlayer(player, plTarget) instead of canHsPlayer(player, pl) when filtering players in 300px radius, and lines 872-873 heal the caster player inside the for (Player pl : players) loop on every iteration.
findings.title: Skill.TRI_THUONG heals enemies and multiplies caster self-heal per target

findings.impact: Players can instant-cast QCKK and Makankosappo without waiting the 4000ms/3000ms charge time by sending back-to-back attack packets (100-150ms apart).
findings.root_cause: useSkillAttack records lastTimePrepareQCKK (line 482) and lastTimePrepareLaze (line 521) when starting preparation, and returns without deducting MP or setting cooldown; on the second call (prepareQCKK/prepareLaze == true), it never validates elapsed time against lastTimePrepareQCKK or lastTimePrepareLaze (unlike TU_SAT at line 772).
findings.title: Missing charge-time validation allows instant-cast QCKK and Makankosappo bypass

findings.impact: Clients can teleport anywhere inside the map bounds in one packet (speed/teleport hack) with zero server-side distance check.
findings.root_cause: playerMove(player, x, y) clamps client-supplied (x, y) only to [24, mapWidth-24] and [24, mapHeight-24] without validating movement delta against lastTimeplayerMove or player speed.
findings.title: Client-trusted coordinates in PlayerService.playerMove allow arbitrary in-map teleportation

findings.impact: Players with >2.14B HP have their HP truncated to 2,147,483,647 on every Kaioken attack, and players with 1-10% HP cannot cast Kaioken despite only needing 1-3% HP.
findings.root_cause: useSkillAttack wraps hpUse and remaining HP (hp - hpUse) in Util.maxIntValue() (line 440) clamping long HP down to Integer.MAX_VALUE; additionally, canUseSkillWithMana (line 1175) requires hp > 10% hpMax while useSkillAttack deducts 1-3% hpMax (and if hp <= hpUse at line 437 it breaks out of switch skipping affterUseSkill while still returning true).
findings.title: Kaioken truncates >2.14B HP to Integer.MAX_VALUE and mismatches mana check (10% vs 1-3%)

findings.impact: Neutral players in public maps (cFlag == 0) get buffed by another player's Huyt Sao, and neutral Namec players lose 10% HP unconditionally without PvP/flag/death checks.
findings.root_cause: useSkillAlone (HUYT_SAO) filters zone.getHumanoids() using only player.cFlag == pl.cFlag without checking cFlag != 0 or canAttackPlayer/isDie, applying Huyt Sao buff or 10% hpMax damage (to Namec) to all neutral players in the zone.
findings.title: Skill.HUYT_SAO affects neutral (cFlag == 0) players and damages neutral Namecs in safe/public maps

findings.impact: Concurrent revive requests can double-deduct gold/gem+ruby or revive a player twice.
findings.root_cause: hoiSinh performs check-then-act on player.isDie(), lastTimeRevived, and inventory gold/gem deduction before calling Service.gI().hsChar without synchronizing on player or inventory.
findings.title: Unsynchronized check-then-act in PlayerService.hoiSinh risks double-spend / double-revive

findings.impact: Potential Netty ByteBuf/Message memory leak on every PlayerService.sendInfoHpMpMoney call and on exception paths in other send methods.
findings.root_cause: sendInfoHpMpMoney never calls msg.cleanup() at all; sendTNSM, sendMessageAllPlayer, sendMessageIgnore, sendInfoHp, sendInfoMp, sendCurrentStamina, sendMaxStamina, and sendTypePk call msg.cleanup() outside a finally block. Conversely, SkillService.learSkillSpecial (lines 377, 382) calls message.cleanup() twice.
findings.title: Missing Message.cleanup() in sendInfoHpMpMoney and non-finally cleanup paths

findings.impact: If status==20 requests switching from a Type-2 skill (Tri Thuong) to another skill, it executes Tri Thuong first and skips switching; Type-4 skills consume MP and trigger cooldown with no combat effect.
findings.root_cause: useSkill evaluates skillSelect.template.type == 2 at line 110 before checking status == 20 skillId switching at line 172; useNewSkillNotFocus (type 4) had special cases removed (line 226) and only calls affterUseSkill.
findings.title: useSkill checks Type-2 buff before status=20 skill switch and Type-4 skills are no-ops with MP/CD cost

findings.impact: Truncating long param in sendTNSM (-3) and target count in newSkillNotFocus (-45) can overflow client-displayed TNSM or drop/corrupt target lists when >127 targets exist.
findings.root_cause: sendTNSM casts long param to int (writeInt((int) param)); newSkillNotFocus casts playersTaget.size() + mobsTaget.size() to signed byte (line 339), causing negative num if >127. Also useSkill (line 86) silently ignores IOException when reading status==20 packet fields.
findings.title: Integer/byte truncation and silent IOException swallow in packet writers/readers

findings.impact: NullPointerException if a banned player has null session (silently swallowed, account not banned in DB) and blocking JDBC call on Netty/game thread.
findings.root_cause: banPlayer accesses playerBaned.getSession().userId/uu without null-checking getSession(), runs AlyraManager.executeUpdate synchronously on caller thread, and swallows all exceptions in an empty catch block.
findings.title: PlayerService.banPlayer lacks session null-check, blocks caller thread, and swallows exceptions

findings.impact: Unnecessary heap allocations (Stream, String arrays, string concatenation) on hot combat loop paths.
findings.root_cause: useSkillAttack allocates zone.getBosses().stream() on every attack (line 418); THAI_DUONG_HA_SAN allocates a new String[] per target inside the loop (line 656); useSkill builds effDesc via String concatenation.
findings.title: Per-attack Stream and per-target String[] allocations in SkillService hot paths

findings.impact: Non-thread-safe singleton and tight coupling across 1487 lines complicate combat maintenance.
findings.root_cause: SkillService.gI() is an unsynchronized non-volatile lazy singleton, and SkillService mixes validation, cooldown/mana accounting, AoE/DoT/reflect/lifesteal combat formulas, PvP rules, and binary Message encoding in one 1487-line class.
findings.title: Non-thread-safe singleton and God-class coupling in SkillService

key_classes.name: PlayerService
key_classes.responsibility: Handles player state updates and packet dispatches for HP/MP/money/stamina/TNSM, movement validation/fly MP cost, daily login reset, PK type changes, account banning, and revival.

key_classes.name: SkillService
key_classes.responsibility: Central combat and skill execution service: validates skill eligibility (mana, cooldown, CC, PvP/PK rules), executes melee/ki/AoE/buff/self-destruct/special skills, computes reflect and lifesteal, and broadcasts combat packets.

module_summary: Read all 1,816 lines across PlayerService.java (329 lines) and SkillService.java (1,487 lines). PlayerService manages player HP/MP/money/stamina/TNSM packets, movement handling, daily reset, PK state, banning, and revival. SkillService is the core combat engine handling skill selection, mana/cooldown checks, PvP rules, damage/reflect/lifesteal execution, and combat packet broadcasts. Direct inspection revealed critical gameplay/security issues including a Tri Thuong targeting/self-heal multiplier bug, missing charge-time enforcement on QCKK and Makankosappo, client-trusted movement coordinates, Kaioken HP int-truncation, Huyt Sao hitting neutral players, unsynchronized revival, and ByteBuf Message.cleanup() leaks.
